# Nebius to increase prices for Nvidia GPU resources from October

Editor Louis Juricic Stock Markets

Editor Louis Juricic

Published Sep 17, 2026, 09:47 AM

© Reuters

Investing.com -- Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1, the company said in an emailed statement, according to Bloomberg News. 

The price increases will apply to Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPU resources, according to the statement. The company will also raise rates for certain CPU and memory resources.

The new pricing structure takes effect at the beginning of next month.

results.title: AI Cloud Firm Nebius Hikes GPU, CPU Prices | Silicon UK Tech
results.author: Matthew Broersma
highlights:
Amsterdam-based AI cloud provider Nebius said on Thursday it would raise prices for renting GPU and CPU capacity, in an indication of sustained demand for training and deploying AI models.

The move came after competitor CoreWeave said earlier in the day that it is signing new contracts at higher prices.

Companies such as Nebius, CoreWeave and Australia’s IREN specialise in cloud capacity for the AI industry, a market that has grown rapidly in recent months.

...

## Price hike

As of 1 October, Nebius said it would charge roughly 17 percent more for Nvidia H100 instances and 21 percent for the newer Nvidia B300, while rates for the AMD Epyc Genoa server CPU would rise by 25 percent.

Memory offerings are to rise by 41 percent, Nebius said.

The hike was Nebius’ second in three months, with pricing for B300 instances rising a cumulative 56 percent.

The company said customers reserving large-scale clusters for multiple months can receive discounts.

results.title: Nebius Is Raising Prices For Nvidia GPU Cloud Access - Finimize
results.author: Finimize Newsroom
highlights:
The neocloud firm will lift pay-as-you-go rates 17%-21% from October 1st, as demand for AI computing keeps tightening supply.

2 mins

What's going on here?

Nebius, a neocloud provider that rents Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) through its AI cloud, says it’ll raise pay-as-you-go prices for some chips on October 1st – its second hike in three months.

What does this mean?

“Neoclouds” sit between Big Tech clouds and companies that would rather not build their own data centers: they bundle scarce AI chips and the infrastructure to run them, then rent that capacity out. Nebius said rates for selected Nvidia GPUs will rise 17%-21%; it’s also lifting prices for some CPU-only, memory, AMD, and Intel offerings. The timing is telling: demand for AI computing is still outpacing supply, and CoreWeave, a rival AI cloud pro..

ud provider, said it’s signing contracts at higher prices too.

When on-demand rates jump, customers face a clearer trade-off between flexibility and certainty. Nebius is leaning into that by offering commitment discounts to clients that reserve large clusters for multiple months, which effectively turns “metered” cloud spending into capacity booked in advance. For providers, that swap can mean slightly less upside from peak pricing, but better utilization and more predictable revenue and cash flow – especially if big buyers keep locking in multi-year deals.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices 20% as supply tightens | Five Nines
results.author: Arjun Mehta
highlights:
By September 16, 2026, the AI neocloud expansion had reached a pricing inflection. BigGo Finance reported that Nebius said it will raise GPU cloud prices by an average of 20 percent from October 1, covering H100, H200, B200 and B300 chips, with B300 rising from $7.85 to $9.50 per GPU-hour. The announcement pushed Nebius shares up nearly 7 percent in after-hours trading.

That increase followed a financing and siting rush that enterprises watched closely. On August 4, 2026, Sharon AI signed a five-year, $373 million contract with a global AI platform customer for AI cloud services, according to tech-insider.org. The first deployment uses 2,048 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs hosted in NEXTDC data centres in Melbourne and Sydney.

...

The latest price signal matters for enterprises purchasing AI compute. Nebius's increase is its second since May, and it follows auction tests where customers paid 15 to 20 percent above the previous maximum listed price for scarce Blackwell capacity. Nebius also said demand visibility now extends beyond 24 months. tech-insider.org reported that committed-contract discounts can reach 60 percent off list price but require multi-year commitments, and recommended hybrid architectures that keep general workloads on hyperscalers while routing GPU-intensive jobs to neoclouds.

# GPU-cloud operator Nebius plans to raise rental rates for NVIDIA H100, H200, B200, and B300 GPUs.

September 17, 2026 · ComputeLabs Research · from the September 17, 2026 edition

Nebius plans to increase GPU rental rates for NVIDIA H100, H200, B200, and B300, according to financialjuice. The update concerns prices charged by the GPU-cloud operator, rather than NVIDIA’s hardware sale prices.

A later Financial_Express daily roundup describes Nebius as raising prices again by 20%. That summary does not provide a model-by-model price schedule or establish that the same percentage applies uniformly to all four GPU models.

The supplied material does not state an effective date, geographic scope, contract duration, or whether existing customer agreements are affected. It also provides no utilization, available-GPU inventory, or revenue figures, so the planned pricing change should not be presented as an already realized financial result.

results.title: GPU Rental Prices Are Rising Again: What the October 2026 Nebius and AWS Changes Mean for Inference Cost
highlights:
After falling in 2025, H100 rental prices rose in 2026. Nebius raised list prices on 1 October and AWS raised Capacity Blocks on 7 October. Here is what the numbers show and how to plan for them.

...

In short

- GPU rental prices fell in 2025 and are rising in 2026. Nebius raised its H100 on-demand price from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour on 1 October 2026.
- AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks prices by about 15% in October. AWS on-demand prices did not change.
- One price index put the median on-demand H100 SXM at $4.20 per GPU-hour on 7 October 2026. Hyperscalers charged a median of $10.53 for the same GPU.
- The "price per GPU-hour" you see is a list price. Your real cost per token depends on utilization, and a half-idle GPU costs twice as much per token.
- Plan for price drift: use commitments for steady load, keep workloads portable, and track cost per token, not cost per hour.

...

## What changed in October 2026

Key point

Two large providers raised GPU prices within a week of each other, reversing the 2025 trend.

The Uvik GPU Price Index (captured 7 October 2026) lists the dated events. On 1 October, Nebius raised H100 on-demand from $3.85 to $4.50 (+17%). It raised H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (+20%). On 7 October, AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks prices by about 15%.

The Nebius pricing page I fetched today matches the new numbers. It lists H100 at $4.50, H200 at $5.40, B200 at $8.50 and B300 at $9.50 per GPU-hour. It also says prices may change at any time.

IntuitionLabs checked AWS on 10 October 2026. The Capacity Blocks rate for P5 (H100) is $5.970 per GPU. In July 2026 it was $5.191 in US regions and $4.720 in other regions. By my calculation from those figures, that is about +15% in the US and about +26.5% elsewhere. AWS says the rates are next scheduled to be updated in January 2027.

Note

Capacity Blocks are reservations, not on-demand. IntuitionLabs warns against using them for cross-provider comparison. AWS on-demand prices did not change in this round.

...

It excludes spot, marketplace, reserved and contract-only prices. For the H100 SXM it found a median of $4.20, a low of $3.20 (Hyperstack and Thunder Compute) and a high of $12.29 (Microsoft Azure).

Split by type, the four hyperscalers had a median of $10.53. The 12 GPU clouds had a median of $3.95. That is a 2.7x gap. Across all GPUs in the index the hyperscaler multiple runs from 1.7x to 2.7x.

...

Commitments change the picture. Uvik says three-year commitments cut H100 prices by 56% to 57% at AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure. That narrows the hyperscaler gap, but only if you can predict three years of demand.

...

- After falling in 2025, GPU rental prices rose in 2026: on 1 October 2026 Nebius raised H100 on-demand from $3.85 to $4.50 (+17%) and H200 from $4.50 to $5.40; AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks by about 15% (a reservation product, not on-demand, which did not change; next update scheduled January 2027).
- The Uvik index (19 providers, 87 public on-demand prices) put the median H100 SXM at $4.20 per GPU-hour on 7 October, with a hyperscaler median of $10.53 versus $3.95 for 12 GPU clouds (2.7x). Three-year commitments cut H100 prices by 56% to 57% at the big three.
- Which provider you rent from matters more than the month you rent in.

results.title: Nebius (NBIS) raises GPU prices up to 21% from October 1
results.author: Dennis Singleton
highlights:
Nebius (NBIS) raises GPU prices up to 21% from October 1

# Nebius (NBIS) is raising GPU rental prices up to 21% on October 1. CoreWeave (CRWV) told bond buyers it is charging more too.

By Dennis Singleton · Markets Writer · September 17, 2026, 5:45 PM ET · Updated November 10, 2026 Make us a preferred source on Google

## Key points

- Nebius raises GPU rental rates from October 1
- Second increase in three months
- Cloud memory rental rate rises about 41%
- The stock gave back most of an 11% jump

Nebius (NBIS) said Thursday it will raise pay-as-you-go prices for renting selected Nvidia (NVDA) chips from October 1, its second increase in three months, Reuters reported. The stock traded as high as $232.85 in the first half hour and gave back most of that gain, closing at $217.99, up 4.1% from Wednesday's $209.37.

The increases run 17% to 21% across the Nvidia lineup. The listed CPU and memory rates rise 25% and about 41%, respectively. Nebius's own public pricing page still listed the current rates on Thursday afternoon, with no notice of the October change.

| Instance | On-demand before Oct. 1 | From Oct. 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100, per GPU-hour | $3.85 | $4.50 |
| H200, per GPU-hour | $4.50 | $5.40 |
| B200, per GPU-hour | $7.15 | $8.50 |
| B300, per GPU-hour | $7.85 | $9.50 |
| EPYC Genoa, per vCPU-hour | $0.012 | $0.015 |
| Genoa memory, per GiB-hour | $0.0032 | $0.0045 |

We confirmed the current H100, H200 and B200 rates against Nebius's published price list. The B300 rate was not listed publicly at the time, and the company quoted it through sales, so that row and the new column came from the reporting rather than from Nebius. Nebius's price list now shows the new rates, including $9.50 for the B300. The steepest increase is the cloud memory rental rate rather than any accelerator, and the Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) EPYC Genoa processor rate rises more than the GPUs as well.

Nebius has the demand to ask. Reuters reported the company recently signed four customer contracts averaging more than $1 billion each, and its AI cloud revenue grew more than 500% year over year in the second quarter.

## CoreWeave disclosed higher pricing the same day

CoreWeave (CRWV) told prospective bond buyers on Thursday morning that it is charging more for capacity too. In the slide deck it furnished with a $3 billion convertible notes offering, CoreWeave put the recent pricing range for short-dated contracts it signed in the third quarter, meaning three to six months, at about $40 million per megawatt. That figure is annualized revenue divided by the power needed to run those clusters, so it is not comparable to a multi-year contract price. The same deck says prices across CoreWeave's product lines rose about 70% in July, and that more than $25 billion of net new customer commitments landed early in the third quarter.

Both companies disclosed higher pricing on the same day, although their figures cover different services and contract terms. The two stocks went opposite ways. CoreWeave closed at $79.88, down 4.2% from Wednesday's $83.35, while Nebius rose and faded. As context, CoreWeave's pricing disclosure came inside a $3 billion convertible notes offering, with a $500 million purchaser option and a program to sell as many as 35 million shares. We cannot establish what drove either move. Nebius did see its own convertible weigh on its stock in August, when a $4.5 billion deal sent the shares down about 10%.

Another listed neocloud, IREN Ltd (IREN), closed at $43.48, up 2.0%. Nebius last reported second-quarter results on August 12. The new Nebius rates take effect October 1.

...

Update, Nov. 11: NYMEX has filed futures contracts on US rental prices for Nvidia's H100 and B200 chips, and the CFTC's review now runs to Jan. 8, 2027. We explain how GPU rental futures would work.

...

### How much is Nebius raising GPU prices?

Between 17% and 21% on the Nvidia accelerators, effective October 1, 2026. The H100 goes to $4.50 an hour from $3.85, the H200 to $5.40 from $4.50, the B200 to $8.50 from $7.15 and the B300 to $9.50 from $7.85. The largest increases are outside the GPUs: the AMD EPYC Genoa processor rate rises 25% per vCPU-hour and the cloud memory rental rate rises about 41% per GiB-hour. These are rental rates for cloud instances, not prices for physical memory chips.

...

Demand for AI computing capacity is outrunning supply. Reuters reported that Nebius recently signed four customer contracts averaging more than $1 billion each and that its AI cloud revenue grew more than 500% year over year in the second quarter. This is the company's second price increase in three months.
